summary: Shoji Mori specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, later serving there as assistant professor (~1979–1987) and professor (~1987–2009). He was also a researcher at the Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture.
Shoju Inaba was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1962) and as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He later held posts at Otani University and Ueno Gakuen University.

Shokin Furuta worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education. He held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1956–1965) and Nihon University (~1965–1981), and directed Matsugaoka Bunko from 1966.
Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Toyo University (attested in 1987 and 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his studies at Taisho University, where he later served as lecturer (1960), assistant professor (1962), and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).
Shoko Takeuchi specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, where he later became a professor emeritus (attested 1987–1995, 2009).

Shoko Watanabe was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernst Leumann and Naoshiro Tsuji. He was a professor at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969), and an assistant professor at Kyushu University (1948–1953).

Shoku Bando is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, he was affiliated with the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoren Ihara specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as an assistant professor at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965, 1977) and was later a member of the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shoryu Katsura specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Kyoto University and the University of Toronto, and served as professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Hōryūji Kangakuin under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. His academic career included faculty posts at Otani University, Shinshu College, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Higuchi is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 1998) and committee member of the Otani Academic Society (attested 2000).

Shoshin Ichishima was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and later professor emeritus at Taisho University, and was a visiting lecturer in Tibetan Buddhism at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University, where he later served as an assistant professor from ~1966 to 2002.

Shoson Miyamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. He served as professor at Toyo University (~1927), the University of Tokyo (1942), Waseda University (~1946–1954), and Komazawa University (~1954–1974).
Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1984–1997) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2006).

Shoyu Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as vice president of Musashino University (~1966–1995) and chairperson of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism (~1989–1995).

Shozen Kumoi specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He taught at Otani University (1948–1981; later emeritus) and became a professor at Bukkyo University in 1982.
Shri Krishna Saksena was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi (both attested 2016).
